candidate_profile.description: The candidate suspects a cost problem and notices that gallons may be more expensive, but the reasoning is incomplete and they do not fully articulate the cost-allocation and pricing distortion.
behaviour_rules: Acknowledge that profit decline with rising sales suggests a cost issue, but do not pursue that insight sharply.
Ask some useful questions on pricing and packaging, but not in a strongly structured sequence.
Notice that plastic gallons may cost more to produce, but explain the labor and overhead implications only partially.
Recognize that the gallon format became popular, but be slow to connect the sales mix shift to underpricing.
Treat pricing and costing as related, but do not clearly explain the per-ounce pricing problem.
Mention that costs may be allocated incorrectly, but do not fully explain why averaging costs across units is flawed.
Give a reasonable but underdeveloped recommendation to revisit pricing and costs.

expected_issues: Only partially prioritizes the cost side.
Does not fully connect higher gallon packaging and labor costs to the declining profit trend.
Understates the importance of the cost allocation problem and the shift toward 60% gallon sales.
Recommendation is directionally reasonable but not well synthesized.
expected_feedback_points: Prioritize the cost side more decisively from the beginning.
Explain more clearly why gallons are likely the source of margin erosion.
Connect per-ounce pricing, packaging cost, labor cost, and sales mix.
State explicitly that shared overhead allocation across cartons and gallons distorts economics.
Conclude more decisively with activity-based costing and repricing.
